body.heading: Pick what to count
paragraphs: Before your walk, choose one thing to count together: red doors, round windows, dogs, bicycles, or anything you like.
Make a guess first. How many do you think you will find? Write the guess down or just remember it.

body.heading: Walk and tally
paragraphs: Walk your usual route with your adult. Every time you spot your thing, make a tally mark on your paper or count on your fingers.
Take turns spotting. If you both see one at the same time, it still counts once. Teamwork makes the counting fair.

body.heading: Compare at the end
paragraphs: At the end of the walk, count up your tally marks. Was your guess close? Guesses do not have to be right to be fun.
Next time, walk the same route and count the same thing. Did the number change? Some things change every day, and some stay the same.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: turn a short walk into a counting game you invent together.

safetyNotes: Stay on pavements and paths, hold hands near roads, and let your adult be in charge of crossing streets.
Watch where you are walking, not just at your paper, so you do not trip.
screenFreeExtension: Count something inside your home instead: stairs, spoons, cushions, or books on one shelf.
takeaway: Counting the same thing on the same walk can give a different answer every day.
